newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan NGOs announce anti-corruption campaign.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan NGOs announce anti-corruption campaign.

text.p: A group of 10 Moroccan non-governmental organisations said on Thursday they would launch an anti-corruption awareness campaign.
"Moroccan associations cannot substitute for the law but they can prevent corruption from becoming commonplace by making people aware", a statement said.

The 10 organisations lobby on such issues as human rights, education, health and women's rights. Their new campaign is headed by the anti-corruption association Transparency Maroc, which applied for legal recognition early this year.

In a separate statement, the independent Moroccan Human Rights Organisation called for urgent reform of the judiciary which "conditions the administration and its role in monitoring elections, respecting human rights and fundamental liberties and ensuring the right application of the law".
This year Morocco launched a nationwide crackdown on smuggling and tax evasion in which a dozen customs and police officials were arrested.

The Washington-based Human Rights Watch said in a recent report: "Not only do government officials at the highest levels intervene in judicial decisions, but well-connected and wealthy families are also able to manipulate the system to their advantage. As a result the judicial system is reportedly corrupt to its core".
